newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures close sharply down ahead of Christmas.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures close sharply down ahead of Christmas.

text.p: NYCE frozen concentrated orange juice futures settled sharply weaker and barely above new contract lows, as cold weather is likely to elude the Florida citrus belt in the near-term, dealers said.

Prices fell the daily 5.00-cent limit in most contracts, hitting fresh life-of-contract lows across the board in early dealings. The market remained sharply lower throughout the day, pressured by a dearth of buying interest and disappointed speculators.
"The forecast last week called for a cold front and people, especially the specs, were looking for that," Celeste Georgakis, an analyst with Dean Witter, said.

The seven-day forecast calls for low temperatures in the upper 30s (degrees Fahrenheit), too warm to damage fruit. Ample supplies projected for the 1996/97 season should also contribute to weakness, market sources said.
The technical outlook remains bearish with the market stuck in a downtrend. Prices have continue to plunge recently, hitting new contract lows without even a hint of a correction.
Georgakis said firm technical support does not exist, although psychological support may be found at today's lows.

March juice ended down 4.50 at 86.20, traded 89.80 to 85.70, a new contract low. Spot January also closed 4.50 lower at 82.90, after falling to a fresh low of 82.30. The back months settled 4.40 to 4.05 lower.
Analysts said prices came off the lows on short-covering ahead of the holiday. The NYCE will be closed until Thursday.
